key_insight: SVC treats each singular-vector channel as a controllable plasticity unit, selectively updating only the channels that best balance new task learning with retention of pretrained knowledge.
engineering_relevance: This offers a principled parameter-efficient continual-learning strategy for domain adaptation of LLMs when preserving prior capabilities is as important as acquiring new ones.
method: Estimate each channel’s adaptation benefit using domain-specific data.
Estimate forgetting cost using a fixed public general-domain corpus as a history-activation proxy.
Select trainable channels with knee-based cost screening, Pareto-front filtering, and Otsu thresholding.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated across four LLM families and eight downstream tasks, and the abstract reports better preservation of pretrained capabilities while maintaining strong downstream performance versus PEFT baselines.
watch_item: The selection pipeline depends on proxy scoring and thresholding choices, so results may be sensitive to corpus choice, scoring quality, and implementation details.
paper_title: Stability-Plasticity Balance via Singular-Vector Selection in LLM Continual Learning
